whatIsIt.eli5: A pattern finder whose window can bend to follow the shape of a thing, like a curvy leaf.
whatIsIt.simple: A Conv whose sampling positions are shifted by learned offsets (predicted from the input), plus a learned mask. It can follow irregular shapes.
whatIsIt.engineer: Offset/mask conv (3k² channels) + torchvision deform_conv2d + BN + SiLU.

whyExists.eli5: Weeds and leaves are not square.
whyExists.simple: Regular grids sample the same pattern everywhere; deformable sampling adapts to object shape and scale.
whyExists.engineer: Adaptive receptive fields (Dai et al., 2017; Zhu et al., 2019).

eli5: Guess where to look for each spot.
Look there instead of on the fixed grid.
simple: A normal conv predicts 2 offsets and 1 mask value for each kernel position.
The main conv samples at the shifted positions, weighted by the mask.
engineer: Offsets initialised to zero, so it starts as a normal conv.

costNote.eli5: Costs more and is slower than a normal pattern finder.
costNote.simple: Extra offset branch (≈27·c1 weights per position for k = 3) and the sampling step is slow on many edge devices and may not export to every runtime. FLOPs shown here are an estimate.
costNote.engineer: Not all export targets support deform_conv2d; latency often much higher than params suggest.
